He was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Library, made Minister of Agriculture, returned to Vice Director of the Palace Library, and advanced to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent duty rectifying the various offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
秘書少監 heads the Palace Library, not the Secretariat; 太常少卿 is the Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not of the Ministry of Rites.
He first served as Collator of the Secretariat, concurrently compiling the National History and examining the Veritable Records.
He first served as Collator of the Palace Library, concurrently compiling the National History and examining the Veritable Records.
秘書省 is the Palace Library (Imperial Library), not the Secretariat.
Your Majesty should also examine the court and thrice ask: Among my ministers, is there no one who slanders the upright, shocks his teacher, hates integrity, and with crooked speech bends policy?
Your Majesty should also examine the court and thrice ask: Among my ministers, is there no one who slanders the upright, alarms my people, hates integrity, and with crooked speech bends policy?
師 in 震驚朕師 (from the Book of Documents) means the multitude, not a teacher.
Retired chief councillors might receive nominal posts, yet every outer appointment is handed out the same way.
Retired executive officials might receive nominal posts, yet every outer appointment is handed out the same way.
執政 denotes the executive officials (assisting councillors, Bureau of Military Affairs heads), not chief councillors.
He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his concurrent posts and given acting duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
He was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Library while retaining his concurrent posts and given acting duty in the Hanlin Academy.
秘書少監 heads the Palace Library; 學士院 is the Hanlin Academy, not the Academy of Scholarly Worthies (集賢院).

He was then made Diarist and acting Vice Minister of War, and for a time also acting Vice Minister of Personnel with duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. One night the emperor summoned him to draft edicts; by the fourth watch all five were finished, and the emperor marveled at his ability.

He was then made Diarist and acting Vice Minister of War, and for a time also acting Vice Minister of Personnel with duty in the Hanlin Academy. One night the emperor summoned him to draft edicts; by the fourth watch all five were finished, and the emperor marveled at his ability.
直學士院 is duty in the Hanlin Academy, not the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
He was promoted to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat with acting duty as Senior Left Bureau Gentleman and acting Hanlin duty officer.
He was promoted to Assistant Editorial Director of the Palace Library with acting duty as Senior Left Bureau Gentleman and acting Hanlin duty officer.
秘書省 is the Palace Library, not the Secretariat.
In the eighth year he was made Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
In the eighth year he was made Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Assisting Civil Councillor.
參知政事 is the Assisting Civil Councillor (vice chief councillor), not a vice director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
In the ninth year he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhai, and asked to retire to his home district.
In the ninth year he was made Assisting Civil Councillor, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhai, and asked to retire to his home district.
參知政事 is the Assisting Civil Councillor, not a vice director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
— in substance he was urging restoration of Prince Gou's princely rank, reduction of Shi Miyuan's posthumous honors, and recall of Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng.
— in substance he was urging restoration of Prince Hong's princely rank, reduction of Shi Miyuan's posthumous honors, and recall of Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng.
皇子竑 is Zhao Hong (竑 hóng); Gou is a misreading.
He was made Vice Minister of Rites with acting charge of the Ministry of Revenue and a concurrent lectureship.
He was made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with acting charge of the Ministry of Revenue and a concurrent lectureship.
太常少卿 is the Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, not of the Ministry of Rites.
Three times he asked to leave the capital; Attendant Gentleman Hong Ziqi and Diary Attendant Wu Yong each submitted memorials urging that he be kept at court.
Three times he asked to leave the capital; Supervising Secretary Hong Ziqi and Diary Attendant Wu Yong each submitted memorials urging that he be kept at court.
給事中 is the Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not an Attendant Gentleman.
He was promoted to Senior Gentleman of the Right and placed in charge of the Yuntai Observatory.
He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel for the Right Attendant Section and placed in charge of the Yuntai Daoist Abbey.
侍右侍郎 is a vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel (Right Attendant Section); 觀 here is a Daoist abbey, not an observatory.
Summoned to court, he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and again appointed Senior Gentleman of the Right.
Summoned to court, he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and again appointed Vice Minister of Personnel for the Right Attendant Section.
侍右侍郎 is a vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, not a 'Senior Gentleman'.
In 1259 (Kaiqing 1) he was summoned to court to administer the Youshen Observatory with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
In 1259 (Kaiqing 1) he was summoned to court to administer the Youshen Daoist Abbey with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
佑神觀 is a Daoist abbey (sinecure), not an observatory.
He was sent out to govern Quanzhou, then again took charge of the Youshen Observatory.
He was sent out to govern Quanzhou, then again took charge of the Youshen Daoist Abbey.
佑神觀 is a Daoist abbey (sinecure), not an observatory.

He became a Palace Library proofreader and instructor at the Yi-Jing-Hui princes' mansion.
秘書省正字 is a Proofreader of the Palace Library, not a Secretariat rectifier.

He was made Palace Library collator and promoted to assistant historiographer.
秘書省 is the Palace Library, not the Secretariat.

He became director of the Palace Library, attendant in the Secret Repository, and prefect of Jizhou.
秘書監 is the Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.

He was then appointed to oversee archival records of the ministries of punishments and works in the Department of State Affairs.
尚書 here is the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat (中書).

In successive posts he served as drafter for the military reward wine warehouse, then supervised personnel ministry archives in the Department of State Affairs.
尚書吏部 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.
